Convergence of a gcTMB fit

Source: R/update.R
converged.Rd

Whether the fit converged to a maximum of the likelihood. A fit that failed with an error and was returned by control=list(onerror="warning") (see gcTMBcontrol) has not converged, with its error as the reason. Otherwise: the negative log-likelihood is finite, the optimiser reports convergence, the Hessian of the parameters is positive definite (not checked for fits with control=list(sdreport=FALSE), see gcTMBcontrol), and the largest absolute gradient is below gradtol. By default, fits with standard deviations of the random effects close to zero count as converged; with singular=TRUE such singular fits do not (a standard deviation below sdtol, or with a standard error of its log that is not finite or above 100, as in summary). Note that the Hessian of a singular fit is often not positive definite.

Usage

converged(
  object,
  gradtol = 0.001,
  singular = FALSE,
  sdtol = 1e-08,
  lltol = 1e-06
)

Arguments

object

A gcTMB object, the result of gcTMB.

gradtol

Numeric. The largest acceptable absolute gradient of the negative log-likelihood, projected on the bounds of the coefficients.

singular

Logical. If TRUE, singular fits, with a standard deviation of the random effects close to zero, count as not converged; FALSE (default) accepts them.

sdtol

Numeric. With singular=TRUE, standard deviations of the random effects below sdtol make the fit singular.

lltol

Numeric. For a fit restarted by control=list(restart=TRUE): if the restart improved the log-likelihood by less than lltol, the optimiser message and the gradient are not checked.

Value

TRUE or FALSE, with the attribute reasons, a character vector of the failed checks (empty for a converged fit). NA for a model with parameters set by update.gcTMB.

Details

A fit with control=list(restart=TRUE) (see gcTMBcontrol) that was optimised a second time from its estimates, and whose log-likelihood the restart improved by less than lltol, is at the maximum: the convergence message of the optimiser and the gradient are then not checked. With few groups and several correlated random effects, the likelihood is often too flat in some directions for nlminb to report convergence or reach a gradient below gradtol, although the maximum is reached.

Examples

fit <- gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, rform=b1 + b2 ~ 1 | Plant_ID, data=FabaHeights25)
converged(fit)
#> [1] TRUE
